title: Normalized rational Chevalley parameters with integral one-sign group laws
statement:
Let $\mathcal R=(M,\Phi,M^\vee,\Phi^\vee)$ be a finite reduced root datum and $(G,T_{\mathbf Q}=D_{\mathbf Q}(M))$ a split realization over $\mathbf Q$ [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. Assume $\mathbf Q\Phi=M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ and $\mathbf Z\Phi^\vee=M^\vee$. There exist a base $\Delta$ and group isomorphisms $p_\alpha:\mathbf G_{a,\mathbf Q}\to U_\alpha\subset G$ for every root, equivariant for $t\cdot z=\chi_\alpha(t)z$, with the following properties. Here $\mathbf G_a(R)=(R,+)$, $\chi_\alpha(t)=t(e^\alpha)$, and the root subgroups are those of [lem-sfb-relative-canonical-root-exponential] over $\mathbf Q$.

Write $T_{\mathbf Z}=D_{\mathbf Z}(M)$ [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group], $\Phi^+$ for the positive roots, and $E_\pm=\prod_{\alpha\in\pm\Phi^+}\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf Z}$ with $\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf Z}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[z]$. Choose one ordering for each product. There are group-scheme structures on $E_\pm$ whose identity is the zero tuple, whose multiplication and inverse are polynomial maps with integer coefficients, and whose generic fibres are identified with the positive and negative unipotent radicals of $G$ by the ordered products of the same $p_\alpha$. For each root in the corresponding sign, the coordinate axis $\mathbf G_{a,\mathbf Z}\to E_\pm$ is a closed group homomorphism [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The action of $T_{\mathbf Z}$ multiplying the $\alpha$ coordinate by $\chi_\alpha(t)$ is by group automorphisms. For every other ordering, multiplication of the coordinate axes in that order is an isomorphism from their product scheme to $E_\pm$, with polynomial inverse over $\mathbf Z$. In particular the integral groups and their torus actions are compatible with all reorderings. A group scheme here has multiplication, inverse and identity satisfying the group diagrams, as in [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization].

For every root $\alpha$ the chosen parameters satisfy, as morphism identities over $\mathbf Q$,
$$p_\alpha(u)p_{-\alpha}(v)=p_{-\alpha}(v/(1+uv))\,\alpha^\vee(1+uv)\,p_\alpha(u/(1+uv))\quad\text{on }D(1+uv),$$
where $D(1+uv)$ is the open locus on which $1+uv$ is a unit and $\alpha^\vee$ is the prescribed monomial cocharacter. For $n_\alpha=p_\alpha(1)p_{-\alpha}(-1)p_\alpha(1)$ one has $n_\alpha p_\alpha(z)n_\alpha^{-1}=p_{-\alpha}(-z)$. More generally $n_\alpha p_\beta(z)n_\alpha^{-1}=p_{s_\alpha\beta}(\epsilon_{\alpha,\beta}z)$ for signs $\epsilon_{\alpha,\beta}\in\{1,-1\}$. These are parameters on the given rational group; no integral reductive model is assumed. Empty roots are allowed, with $E_+=E_-=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition 6.3.4 and the normalization following Remark 6.3.5; Lemmas 6.3.6--6.3.7, printed pp.215--220. Rank-one normalization: Theorem 4.2.6(1), equation (4.2.1), Corollary 5.1.9(3). Read online; WANTED local copy. This is the integral one-sign coordinate input, not a partial law on the full root cell. No Stacks tag states it.

proof.text: Extend the lattice pairing to $M_{\mathbf Q}\times M^\vee_{\mathbf Q}$. The roots span by hypothesis and the coroots span because they generate $M^\vee$. Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-rational-root-pairing-base] to choose $\Delta$; choose a nonzero vector in each simple root line. Write $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{Lie}(T_{\mathbf Q})$ and $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ with the bracket of [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus]. Over $\overline{\mathbf Q}$, [lem-sfb-semisimple-roots-span] makes $G$ semisimple and [lem-sfb-char-zero-semisimple-group-lie] makes its Lie algebra semisimple. The scalar-extension identification in the tangent-calculus node now proves that $\mathfrak g$ is semisimple over $\mathbf Q$: a solvable rational ideal tensors to a solvable ideal, since each term of its derived series tensors to the corresponding bracket span, and a nonzero rational vector remains nonzero after field extension. The torus weight decomposition in the split realization differentiates to the $\mathfrak h$-root decomposition: $G$ is smooth, connected and affine of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, so $d\operatorname{Ad}_e(X)=\operatorname{ad}X$ by [lem-sfb-charzero-adjoint-differential-central-kernel]. Evaluating $\operatorname{Ad}(t)v=\chi_m(t)v$ for $v\in\mathfrak g_m$ at the dual-number point $t=1+\epsilon X$ of $T$, $X\in\mathfrak h$, gives $[X,v]=d\chi_m(X)v$; for $m=0$ and $v\in\mathfrak h$ this gives $[X,v]=0$, since $T$ is commutative. Distinct lattice characters have distinct differentials in characteristic zero. Its zero-weight space is $\mathfrak h$, so $\mathfrak h$ is maximal abelian and acts diagonally. Thus it is a splitting Cartan algebra in the convention of the Chevalley-normalization lemma.

source.place: Example 6.3.3, pp.214--215; characteristic-zero rational descent written out by Q103

proof.text: The coroot in the Lie algebra is the differential of the prescribed group coroot. Indeed, for each root take its rank-one centralizer $H$ [lem-sfb-relative-root-rank-one-centralizer]. Over an algebraically closed field $F\supseteq\mathbf Q$, $H_F$ is the centralizer of $T_\alpha=\ker\chi_{\alpha_0}$, which is the largest subtorus of $\ker\chi_\alpha$ because $\ker\chi_\alpha/T_\alpha\cong\mu_d$ is finite. So [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections] shows that $H_F$ has semisimple rank one, the remaining hypothesis of the matrix model over $\mathbf Q$ [lem-sfb-relative-rank-one-local-matrix-model]. In that model, conjugation by the antidiagonal matrix swaps the diagonal entries, i.e. acts by $t\mapsto t\lambda(\chi_\alpha(t))^{-1}$ with $\lambda(s)=\operatorname{diag}(s,s^{-1})$. By the uniqueness of the reflection cocharacter in [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], applied over $F$ (monomial cocharacters of the split torus are determined after scalar extension), $\lambda$ is the prescribed coroot $\alpha^\vee$. In that model the two root lines are the $E_{12},E_{21}$ lines and their bracket is $\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$; this is the differential of $s\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(s,s^{-1})$, with root value $2$. The central torus contributes zero. The computation survives the scalar quotient in the $\operatorname{PGL}_2$ case. Consequently [lem-sfb-chevalley-root-normalization] gives rational vectors $e_\alpha$ extending our simple choices and satisfying $[e_\alpha,e_{-\alpha}]=h_\alpha=d\alpha^\vee(1)$, with all its Chevalley bracket constants. Define $p_\alpha(z)=\exp_\alpha(ze_\alpha)$ using [lem-sfb-relative-canonical-root-exponential]. This is an isomorphism from $\mathbf G_a$ onto the stated root subgroup and is equivariant for the full character $\chi_\alpha$. The same fixed vectors and these same maps are used in all the subsequent steps.

source.place: Example 6.3.3, Proposition 6.3.4 and the opposite-root normalization on p.217; Theorem 4.2.6(1)

proof.text: In the rank-one matrix model from step 2, write the images of $e_\alpha,e_{-\alpha}$ as $cE_{12},dE_{21}$. Their bracket normalization says $cd=1$. Canonical-root uniqueness identifies $p_\alpha(u)$ and $p_{-\alpha}(v)$ with the images of $I+cuE_{12}$ and $I+c^{-1}vE_{21}$, respectively. Put $w=1+uv$. Direct matrix multiplication gives $x_c(u)y_c(v)=y_c(v/w)\operatorname{diag}(w,w^{-1})x_c(u/w)$, where $x_c(u)=I+cuE_{12}$ and $y_c(v)=I+c^{-1}vE_{21}$; both sides have entries $(1+uv,cu,c^{-1}v,1)$ in row-major order, in $\mathbf Q[u,v,w^{-1}]$. The middle matrix gives the prescribed $\alpha^\vee(w)$: this is the group coroot, whose differential was identified in step 2, and monomial cocharacters in characteristic zero are determined by their integer differentials. The same identity holds in the central product and scalar quotient models. The product defining $n_\alpha$ is the image of the matrix with row-major entries $(0,c,-c^{-1},0)$; it normalizes the diagonal torus and conjugates $I+czE_{12}$ to $I-c^{-1}zE_{21}$. Hence the opposite-root and minus-sign identities of the item hold as morphism identities, without restricting to field-valued points.

source.place: Theorem 4.2.6(1), equation (4.2.1), Corollary 5.1.9(3); explicit matrix calculation by Q103

proof.text: Choose a closed faithful representation $r:G\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}(W)$ by [lem-sfb-affine-group-faithful-linear-representation], and differentiate it using [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus]. Apply [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis] successively to the factors of the split torus. The factors commute, so each preserves the previous weight spaces, giving a finite rational character decomposition $W=\bigoplus_\lambda W_\lambda$, $\lambda\in M$. Let $E_\alpha=dr(e_\alpha)$. Differentiating equivariance shows that $E_\alpha(W_\lambda)\subset W_{\lambda+\alpha}$. Thus $E_\alpha$ is nilpotent, since only finitely many weights occur and $\alpha\ne0$ in the torsion-free lattice $M$. The simple coroot operators act on $W_\lambda$ by integers $\langle\lambda,\delta^\vee\rangle$. For later use, a polynomial one-parameter matrix group $A(z)=\sum A_jz^j$ with $A(0)=I$ satisfies $A'(z)=A(z)A_1$, by differentiating $A(z+t)=A(z)A(t)$ at $t=0$. Coefficient comparison yields $A_j=A_1^j/j!$. Applying this to $r p_\alpha$ gives $r(p_\alpha(z))=\sum E_\alpha^jz^j/j!$ as polynomial identities over $\mathbf Q$.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.7, coefficient-integrality input; rational representation realization of the root parameters, Q103

proof.text: Here is the lattice argument needed to apply the existing matrix commutator node. Choose a rational weight basis of $W$ and let $L_0$ be its integer span. Let $U_{\mathbf Z}$ be the divided-power algebra of [lem-sfb-kostant-integral-pbw] for our Chevalley basis, acting through $dr$, and set $L=U_{\mathbf Z}L_0$. This subgroup contains $L_0$ and is stable under every $E_\alpha^j/j!$ by its definition. It is finitely generated over $\mathbf Z$: the PBW node expresses its generators as ordered negative-root divided powers, followed by simple-coroot binomials, followed by ordered positive-root divided powers, applied to weight-basis vectors. Each root exponent has a uniform upper bound from nilpotence of its operator. For each of the finitely many resulting positive words, its value is a weight vector; all the middle binomials act on it by integers $\binom{a}{b}$ with $a\in\mathbf Z$, including $a<0$. Thus varying the middle exponents introduces only integer multiples, and the finitely many bounded positive and negative words generate $L$. These generating vectors are weight homogeneous, so $L=\bigoplus_\lambda(L\cap W_\lambda)$. A finitely generated subgroup of the rational vector space $W$ containing a rational basis is a full lattice: writing the finite generators in that basis and multiplying by a common denominator puts it between $L_0$ and $d^{-1}L_0$. Apply [lem-sfb-pid-submodule-smith-bases] to the submodule $L$ of the finite free integer module $d^{-1}L_0$ to see that $L$ is finite free. Containment of the rational basis shows its rank is $\dim W$ and $L\otimes\mathbf Q=W$. This uses an actual lattice construction, not the existence of an integral reductive group.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.7, pp.218--219; agent-written PBW verification for its coefficient-integrality input

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-chevalley-nonopposite-exponential-commutator] to $\mathfrak g$, the representation $dr$ and the full lattice $L$ constructed in step 5. Its hypotheses require neither the representation's weights to generate the weight lattice nor an already constructed Chevalley group. For distinct, nonopposite roots it gives integer constants and a polynomial matrix identity
$$[r p_\alpha(u),r p_\beta(v)]=\prod_{i,j>0}r p_{i\alpha+j\beta}(C_{i,j}u^iv^j).$$
By the injectivity on all algebra-valued points in [lem-sfb-affine-group-faithful-linear-representation], this is the corresponding identity in $G$ over every $\mathbf Q$-algebra. Every correction root has height strictly greater than either input root in a single positive system. This is the integral local interchange relation needed below; it has not assumed any integral group law.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.7, equation (6.3.3), p.219; existing Chevalley matrix commutator supplies the rank-two coefficient input

proof.text:
Order the positive roots $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_N$ by nondecreasing height. Every tail $\Psi_i=\{\alpha_i,\ldots,\alpha_N\}$ is closed under root sums, since a sum has strictly greater height than either summand. By [lem-sfb-split-root-subgroup-weyl-calculus], its ordered product is a rational subgroup with these unique coordinates. We construct integral laws for the tails by descending induction. The empty tail is the trivial group. Suppose the law and inverse on the tail $i+1$ are integral. Put $a=\alpha_i$. For each later root $b$, step 6 expresses $p_a(-s)p_b(z)p_a(s)$ as a finite product of later-root parameters with integer polynomial arguments: its commutator factors have roots $ja+kb$ of height greater than that of $b$, followed by $p_b(z)$. Evaluate this product with the known tail law, and multiply the resulting expressions for all the later coordinates. This constructs an integer polynomial map $C_s(x)$ which over $\mathbf Q$ is $p_a(-s)x p_a(s)$ on the later tail. Writing the $i$-tail as $p_a(u)x$, define
$$(u,x)(v,y)=(u+v,C_v(x)y),\qquad (u,x)^{-1}=(-u,C_{-u}(x^{-1})).$$
Both maps have integer coefficients by the induction hypothesis and the construction of $C$. Their rational fibres are precisely multiplication and inversion, as follows by moving $p_a(v)$ to the left. Their identity is $(0,0)$. This proves the induction for every tail. Apply the identical construction to $-\Phi^+$, giving $-\alpha$ the positive height of $\alpha$; step 6 applies to those roots too. We have constructed the required operations on $E_+$ and $E_-$.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.7, descending tail induction on p.219; explicit semidirect-coordinate formulas by Q103

proof.text: All group diagrams for these operations are polynomial identities over $\mathbf Z$, true over $\mathbf Q$ by their construction. The injection $\mathbf Z[\mathbf z]\hookrightarrow\mathbf Q[\mathbf z]$ proves each diagram integrally. Each coordinate axis is a closed immersion: on coordinate rings its restriction sends its own coordinate to $z$ and all others to zero, and is surjective [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its homomorphism identity is again an integral polynomial identity true rationally. The diagonal torus action on coordinates is defined over $\mathbf Z$ by [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. The identities saying that this action preserves multiplication, identity and inverse hold rationally by root equivariance, and hence integrally by the injection $\mathbf Z[M][\mathbf z]\hookrightarrow\mathbf Q[M][\mathbf z]$. Thus it acts by group automorphisms. Finally, [lem-sfb-relative-root-product-open-cell] over $A=\mathbf Q$ identifies the generic positive and negative products with the corresponding unipotent radicals; its hypotheses hold for $H=G$ and $S=T\simeq\mathbf G_{m,\mathbf Q}^r$ after a lattice basis of $M$ is chosen. For the functional take an integer multiple of the linear form on $M_{\mathbf Q}$ equal to $1$ on $\Delta$; it is positive exactly on $\Phi^+$. Its root subgroups $U_\alpha$ and those of step 2 are closed subgroups of $G$ with the same base change to an algebraic closure, namely the root subgroups there. Hence they are equal, because the ideals of closed subschemes are recovered after the faithfully flat field extension.

source.place: Paragraph following Lemma 6.3.7, pp.219--220; polynomial and Laurent-polynomial identities written out by Q103

proof.text:
Fix any other ordering and multiply the integral coordinate axes in that order using the laws just constructed. This gives an integer polynomial map $F:E_\pm\to E_\pm$. It is torus equivariant by step 8. Give each signed root the positive height used in step 7. Independence of the monomials $e^m$ in $\mathbf Z[M]$ says that the output coordinate $F_\gamma$ contains only monomials of full root weight $\gamma$. There is no constant term, and its only possible linear term is $z_\gamma$; setting every other input coordinate to zero shows its coefficient is $1$. Every variable in a nonlinear monomial of weight $\gamma$ has strictly smaller positive height than $\gamma$, because all variable heights are positive and sum to that height. Therefore
$$F_\gamma=z_\gamma+P_\gamma((z_\eta)_{\mathrm{ht}(\eta)<\mathrm{ht}(\gamma)}),\qquad P_\gamma\in\mathbf Z[\mathbf z].$$
Recursively in height, solve $z_\gamma=w_\gamma-P_\gamma((z_\eta)_{\mathrm{ht}(\eta)<\mathrm{ht}(\gamma)})$. This is an integer polynomial inverse to $F$ in both directions, as direct substitution shows. Consequently multiplication in every ordering is an isomorphism, and the transition maps intertwine the same group operations and torus actions. This proves all the reordering clauses directly, without invoking a separate integral direct-spanning theorem.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.6 and its use after Lemma 6.3.7; agent-written triangular proof in the present polynomial coordinate situation

proof.text:
It remains to verify the general Weyl-sign clause for these same parameters. Apply the coefficient recursion of step 4 to the polynomial matrix homomorphism $\operatorname{Ad}\circ p_\alpha$ on $\mathfrak g$. Its differential is $\operatorname{ad}(e_\alpha)$ by [lem-sfb-charzero-adjoint-differential-central-kernel]; nilpotence is provided by [lem-sfb-split-semisimple-root-decomposition]. Hence
$$\operatorname{Ad}(n_\alpha)=\exp(\operatorname{ad}e_\alpha)\exp(-\operatorname{ad}e_{-\alpha})\exp(\operatorname{ad}e_\alpha).$$
By [lem-sfb-chevalley-adjoint-weyl-signs], this sends $e_\beta$ to $\epsilon_{\alpha,\beta}e_{s_\alpha\beta}$ for a sign. Step 3 gives that $n_\alpha$ normalizes the full torus and induces $s_\alpha$. Thus $n_\alpha p_\beta(z)n_\alpha^{-1}$ is equivariant for the root character $s_\alpha\beta$ and has that tangent vector. Uniqueness in [lem-sfb-relative-canonical-root-exponential], with the parameter rescaled by the indicated sign, proves
$$n_\alpha p_\beta(z)n_\alpha^{-1}=p_{s_\alpha\beta}(\epsilon_{\alpha,\beta}z).$$
This is uniqueness of group-scheme maps, so it proves the identity on all rational algebra-valued points, including nonreduced algebras.

source.place: Definition 6.3.2, Example 6.3.3, Corollary 5.1.9(3), proof of Lemma 6.3.8; adjoint-to-group verification by Q103

proof.text: If $\Phi$ is empty, the spanning assumption gives $M=0$. Choose the empty base and empty family of parameters. Each $E_\pm$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with its unique group law, the torus action is trivial, and the ordering and root-indexed identities are vacuous. The root-product statement used in step 8 identifies its generic fibre with the trivial unipotent radical. Thus the construction includes rank zero.

source.place: Empty-root case, checked directly by Q103

proof_origin.place: Q103 proof following the one-sign construction of Conrad, Lemma 6.3.7, with the existing Chevalley-basis/PBW commutator route and explicit triangular reordering argument. Source read online; local copy WANTED.
